clue.text: Something we all have in common

definitions.text: Something we all have in common

parts.words: Something we all have in common
parts.note: reads like a shared trait of humanity, but means a thing owned jointly by everyone, like a park or a public road

explanation.surface: A remark about a trait shared by every human being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In common' sounds like shared character, but here it means held in common ownership by the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Things owned by the community at large, such as parks, belong to every citizen jointly.

clue.text: Two girls, one on each knee

parts.note: Pat is a girl's name
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Two young women sit one on each of someone's knees.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures girls perched on knees; the definition is the bone found at the front of each knee.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap is the small flat bone at the front of every knee joint, so there is one per knee.

clue.text: To have to run away from the police is an unexpected occurrence

parts.note: to bolt is to run off suddenly
taken as written
police officers wear blue uniforms, hence 'the boys in blue', the blue

explanation.surface: Having to flee from the police is a surprising turn of events.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BLUE stands for the police, from their blue uniforms; the whole phrase means lightning from a clear sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom compares a sudden shock to lightning striking from a clear sky.

clue.text: I make an offer in place of a previous quotation

definitions.text: in place of a previous quotation

parts.note: to bid is to make an offer, as at an auction

explanation.surface: Someone at an auction speaks up with an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation, from Latin ibidem 'in the same place', is used in footnotes to refer back to a source already cited.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin footnote abbreviation means 'the same source' and stands instead of repeating the citation given just before.

clue.text: Neglect Dad's drink

parts.note: Pa is a word for dad, so dad's gives PA'S
to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: A comment about Father's beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: To let an opportunity go by is to neglect or decline it.

clue.text: Got into a bed made incorrectly

indicators.note: a bed made badly suggests these letters are put together in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone climbed into a bed whose sheets were badly made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made incorrectly' reads as poor bed-making but tells you to rearrange INTO A BED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have acquired something is to have got it.

clue.text: Like an astronaut returning-or failing to get lift-off?

definitions.meaning: a spacecraft coming home is heading towards our planet, bound for it
something that cannot leave the ground is stuck on our planet

explanation.surface: Musing on spacemen coming home, or on rockets that never left the pad.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of 'bound': heading for a place, and tied down to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound means both heading for our planet and confined to its surface, covering a homecoming astronaut and a grounded rocket.

clue.text: Go under an assumed name

parts.note: describes making a journey while disguised, using a false identity

explanation.surface: Advice to someone who wants to avoid recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' can mean make a journey, and doing so under a false name is moving about in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Journeying while concealing one's real identity is the meaning of this phrase.

clue.text: Sure to change one's ways

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are told to alter their order

explanation.surface: Someone is certain to alter their habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like reform of habits but signals an anagram of SURE TO; 'one's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Paths or courses taken to reach a place are ways of getting there.

clue.text: Last treat for friends at matches

indicators.note: the final letter of the word treat is taken

parts.note: allies are friends or supporters

explanation.surface: A final gift for one's mates at the football games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matches' looks like sporting fixtures, but here it is a verb: to tally is to correspond.
explanation.definitionFit: When two accounts agree or correspond, one is said to tally with the other.

clue.text: Rent row causes a storm

parts.note: rent is an old past participle of rend, meaning torn
a row or fuss is ado

explanation.surface: A dispute over rent payments stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a landlord's charge but is the past of rend, torn.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent whirling windstorm is a kind of storm.

clue.text: Possibly felt that it's not right

indicators.note: signals that the letters of the word felt may be put into another order

explanation.surface: Someone sensed that something was amiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' reads as wrong, but means the opposite of the right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: The side opposite to right is its directional counterpart.

clue.text: Dostoevsky's partner in crime

parts.note: the Russian novelist's best-known title pairs Crime with another word; 'partner in crime' plays on the idiom for an accomplice

explanation.surface: A query about who helped the Russian novelist commit an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: Dostoevsky wrote the novel 'Crime and ...'; the partner of 'Crime' in that title is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the title of the famous Russian novel, the word paired with Crime is the penalty that follows wrongdoing.

clue.text: Genius that outshines all others

parts.note: describes outstanding talent, and also light so strong it is brighter than everything near it

explanation.surface: Praise for a mind more gifted than any rival's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outshines' works literally (being brightest) and figuratively (being most talented).
explanation.definitionFit: Exceptional talent and dazzling brightness are both senses of the noun.

clue.text: Sailor with relevant equipment takes five hundred on the ship

parts.note: AB is able seaman, a common term for a sailor
an oar is equipment relevant to a sailor
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A seaman brings his gear and five hundred pounds aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relevant equipment' means kit relevant to the sailor: the oar.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a ship or other vessel is being on board it.

clue.text: Crimes put one's life in jeopardy

indicators.note: something in jeopardy is in danger of being thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive's s is used as a letter of the fodder here

explanation.surface: Serious offences may endanger the offender's own life.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of ONE'S LIFE, keeping the S of the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious offences, graver than misdemeanours, are crimes of the worst kind.

clue.text: Near the avenue

definitions.meaning: to near something is to come closer to it
the drive or road leading up to a large house

explanation.surface: Directions telling someone they are close to the tree-lined road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' is a verb here, to come closer; 'avenue' is the road leading to a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming closer is drawing nearer, and the drive leading to a house is its way in.

clue.text: Bet a long leaping stride is natural to it

definitions.text: Bet a long leaping stride is natural to it

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up before a hand of poker
a lope is a long bounding stride

explanation.surface: A wager that bounding strides come naturally to some creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a swift African grazing animal that moves in leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: This graceful horned grazer of the savanna is known for its leaping, bounding run.

clue.text: Is this where the Ark went fast?

definitions.text: Is this where the Ark went fast?

parts.words: Is this where the Ark went fast?
parts.note: 'went fast' seems to mean sped, but means became stuck fast, grounded on a mountain

explanation.surface: A question about where Noah's vessel picked up speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' means firmly fixed: in Genesis the Ark came to rest on a Turkish mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Noah's vessel ran aground on this Turkish mountain when the flood receded.

clue.text: Slightly deflects the ball and scores

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to touch the ball off the edge of the bat is to give it a fine deflection
small cuts or notches made in a surface

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman edges the ball and gets runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman whose bat just touches the ball sends it off at a slight angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A light edge off a cricket bat and small cuts or notches share one word, the noun's plural also meaning scores.

clue.text: Not well away from land

parts.note: seems to mean not far offshore, but means unwell when out on the water

explanation.surface: A remark on being close to the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'not well' as ill and 'away from land' as out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea caused by a ship's motion afflicts those out on the waves.

clue.text: Saint gets response in church from organ

parts.note: amen is the congregation's response to a prayer

explanation.surface: A saint hears the congregation answer from the church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' looks like the church instrument but is a part of a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollen-bearing male part of a flower is a plant organ.

clue.text: Better order meal before I make speech

indicators.note: to order something is to put it into a new arrangement

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: Someone orders food and then gives a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like asking for food at a restaurant but is the anagram signal; 'before' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve a situation is to make it better.

clue.text: Site in India, grave of Shah Jahan's wife

indicators.note: the word in tells you the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A tourist note on an Indian monument to an emperor's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail 'of Shah Jahan's wife' completes the picture: the Taj Mahal, Mumtaz Mahal's tomb, stands in this city.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location, and this northern Indian city is the location of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Journey in South Africa

parts.note: an Afrikaans word for a long overland journey, especially by ox-wagon

explanation.surface: A travel note about a journey across South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from Afrikaans, where it described long ox-wagon migrations such as the Great one of the 1830s.
explanation.definitionFit: This Afrikaans word for a long, hard overland migration by wagon is now used for any arduous journey.

clue.text: State capital of Natal at variance

indicators.note: being at variance means differing, so these letters are set in a different order

explanation.surface: The capital of the South African province of Natal is in dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Natal suggests South Africa, but the anagram of NATAL AT gives the capital of Georgia in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the seat of government of the US state of Georgia.

clue.text: Swallow one drink that is an aperitif

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Gulp down one cocktail before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb, to gulp, but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin and vermouth cocktail is typically served before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Chatter-box?

parts.note: a chatterbox is a talkative person, but read literally it is a box one chatters in

explanation.surface: A one-word description of a talkative person.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word: a box to chatter in, a public booth for making calls.
explanation.definitionFit: A street booth housing a public phone is a booth where people talk.
